items.title: A shipped order is labelled Delayed on its promised date
items.hit: Says that on the promised date itself (from 00:00 UTC of that date) a shipped order already shows Delayed, or that the date-only promisedAt is parsed as an instant and compared with the current instant, against the brief's 'from the day after'.
items.partial: Raises a time-zone or date-parsing risk in the comparison without connecting it to the promised-date rule.

items.title: The CSV export still prints Shipped for a delayed order
items.hit: Says the export (src/orders/export.js, toCsv) was not changed and still uses statusLabel, so the requirement that the export shows the same label is not met.

items.title: The missing-status fallback, the Unknown branch and fallbackLabel cannot be reached
items.hit: Calls at least one of `order.status ?? "unknown"`, the Unknown branch or the fallbackLabel option unnecessary AND grounds it in the contract (status required, enum) or in fetchOrders rejecting invalid orders.
items.partial: Calls one of them unnecessary or unused (for instance: no caller passes fallbackLabel) without citing the contract or the validating client.

items.title: The try/catch around new Date can never catch
items.hit: Says the Date constructor does not throw for a string, so the catch is dead code.

items.title: The label table has a second owner and the Delayed rule sits where the export cannot use it
items.hit: Points at LABELS in badge.js duplicating STATUS_LABELS in labels.js, or at the rule living in a unit the export does not call, and proposes one owner used by both the list and the export.
items.partial: Notes the duplicated table without a consequence or a single-owner proposal.

items.title: The tests miss the promised-date boundary and the export, and pin behaviour the contract excludes
items.hit: Names at least one concrete regression the tests would let through: the label on the promised date itself, a shipped order with a null promisedAt, or the export's label; or says the Unknown/fallbackLabel tests pin unreachable behaviour.
items.partial: Asks for more edge-case tests without naming the case.

items.title: Removing the promisedAt null check
items.violated: Recommends removing the null check on promisedAt or states that promisedAt cannot be null for a shipped order. The contract allows null whatever the status; without the check `new Date(null)` is 1970 and the order shows Delayed.

items.title: More defensive handling of malformed orders
items.violated: Recommends, as a finding or a change to make, validating the order's shape or guarding against invalid date strings inside badge.js or list.js. fetchOrders is the only source and already rejects them.
